Summarise indicators over each household's reference period

Source: R/summarise_by_interview.R
summarise_by_interview.Rd

For every survey unit (household), summarises the daily (or monthly) indicators of its location over the window before its interview: the number of hot days in the 12 months before the interview, the longest dry spell in the last rainy season, and so on. Replaces extr_day_by_interview(), extr_spell_by_interview(), extr_day_index() and extr_spell_index().

Usage

summarise_by_interview(
  survey,
  x,
  window = NULL,
  interval = NULL,
  n_lags = 0,
  by = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  interview = NULL,
  extra_col = NULL,
  stats = NULL,
  min_coverage = 0.8,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto"
)

Arguments

survey

The survey, typically from prepare_coord().

x

A long indicator table, e.g. from calc_threshold_day() and calc_spell().

window

A window from window_lag(), window_season(), window_fixed() or window_since().

interval, n_lags

Shortcut for window = window_lag(interval, n_lags).

by

Column linking the survey to x; by default the key of x.

id

<data-masking> Column identifying the survey units; by default the one recorded by prepare_coord().

interview

<data-masking> Interview dates: a column, or one date for everyone; by default the recorded column.

extra_col

<tidy-select> Survey columns to carry into the result.

stats

Optional named list of statistics per kind of indicator, e.g. list(flag = c("sum", "mean"), spell = "max"). Statistics: "sum", "mean", "max", "min", "n" (number of non-missing values).

min_coverage

Share of the window that must be covered by data.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" splits the work by unit when it would not fit in memory; a whole number forces that many units per chunk; FALSE never splits.

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per survey unit and lag: the unit identifier, lag, the extra columns and one column per indicator and statistic (day_abv_30_sum, spell_abv_30_max), registered with the window.

Details

The summaries follow the kind of each indicator in the registry: flags and excesses are summed (days, degree-days), spells give their maximum, mean, sum and count, standardised indices their mean. stats changes this per kind.

A window with less than min_coverage of its days (months for monthly data) present in the data gives NA rather than a count that looks complete but is not, for example a window reaching before the start of the data. Households without an interview date are left out and counted in a message.

The computation runs once per location and interview date and is then given to every household sharing them, and it is split by location when it would exceed the memory budget.

See also

window_lag(), summarise_by_period()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat, lon, id = hhid, interview = interview)

hot <- extract_by_coord(tmax, georef_coord(coord)) |>
  convert_unit("C") |>
  calc_threshold_day(above = 30) |>
  calc_spell()
#> Taking the coordinates as longitude and latitude in "EPSG:4326"; give `crs`
#> otherwise.
#> Using `from = "K"` from upstream unit.
#> Using `unit = "C"` from upstream unit.

summarise_by_interview(coord, hot, interval = "1 year", n_lags = 1)
#> # A tibble: 40 × 8
#> # Context:  tmax [C], day, summary; key hhid; 6 indicators
#>    hhid    lag day_abv_30_sum C_abv_30_sum spell_abv_30_max spell_abv_30_mean
#>    <chr> <int>          <dbl>        <dbl>            <dbl>             <dbl>
#>  1 HH01      0            103         235.               29              8.31
#>  2 HH01      1             97         248.                9              4.31
#>  3 HH02      0            140         419.               38              8.31
#>  4 HH02      1            136         357.               70              8.79
#>  5 HH03      0            105         233.               22              5.88
#>  6 HH03      1             94         209.               20              4.35
#>  7 HH04      0             81         153.               13              4.29
#>  8 HH04      1             86         167.                9              3.63
#>  9 HH05      0            121         277.               57              8.67
#> 10 HH05      1            116         306.               31              6.8 
#> # ℹ 30 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: spell_abv_30_sum <dbl>, spell_abv_30_n <int>
